transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Lena Torres (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Crestline Head of ML), Tom Garcia (Platform), Aisha Clarke (Security), Derek Huang (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto): finalizing rollout plan, agree rollback thresholds, staging dry-run week, collect traffic profiles and security confirmation.

[00:00] Lena: ok hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, appreciate it. quick check, is this still a hard stop at 15:05 UTC for Aisha?
[00:10] Aisha: yeah I gotta jump at 15:05, um but dery, Derek will stay for the rest.
[00:18] Priya: good, thanks. we wanted to make sure the canary thresholds actually protect our clinical path for inference latency and hallucination rate, that's the main worry.
[00:28] Marcus: totally, the focus today is to lock down thresholds, the ramp plan, and the rollback triggers; we'll also propose a dry-run schedule.
[00:41] Tom: quick context, in prod our 95th pct is around 220ms, 99th sits at 480ms, and we have diurnal spikes at 09:00 UTC and 01:00 UTC. most traffic is short prompts around 30 tokens.
[00:58] Lena: perfect, that helps. Marcus, do you have the suggested canary percentages and timing?
[01:12] Marcus: yeah so initial proposal: staging dry-run 5% for 4 hours, then canary in prod 1% for 15 mins, bump to 5% for 30 mins, then 20% for 2 hours, monitor SLOs then 50% for 1 hour before full cut. The gating metrics: 99th latency compared to baseline (no more than +40%), error rate under 0.5% absolute, and a quality regression metric (we'll use the prompt set of 250 golden queries — Priya you'll confirm).
[01:40] Priya: the 250 set is good but we need separate health-care-critical queries flagged; some outputs need exact matching.
[01:50] Marcus: noted, we'll parameterize the eval set to weight critical queries higher. also suggest a fallback model route: if quality spike > threshold, traffic auto-fails over to the older model pinned in Redwood Dedicatd — sorry, Redwood Dedicated pin, or to our in-house low-latency endpoint.
[02:10] Tom: any cost impact for keeping older model around as fallback? we want to estimate incremental dollars.
[02:18] Lena: we can provide a cost delta; for dedicated the retention of a fallback replica is minor relative to outages but we'll quantify.
[02:25] Derek: on the infra side, we need a circuit breaker at the router level when token generation latency crosses 800ms for five consecutive seconds. that prevented the last outage.
[02:35] Marcus: ok we can wire a circuit breaker and create a temporary traffic hold that even does 0% routing to the new model after N failures, and a manual confirm step to resume.
[02:45] Aisha: security question — how are tokens and logs handled during canary? do we retain full request logs in Redwood console? our policy says only audit logs, no full PII retention.
[02:58] Lena: Redwood will set retention to 30 days by default for SE trial; we can set event-level audit only, and integrate with your KMS for key management. we'll send the security checklist doc after.
[03:10] Aisha: also need to confirm SSO and RBAC mappings for the console users.
[03:16] Lena: yes, SAML SSO works; we'll add roles for 'ops' and 'viewer' as discussed.
[03:22] Tom: back to canary: how do we measure semantic quality in near real-time? we cannot wait 24 hours to label outputs.
[03:31] Marcus: we'll use a combination: 1) automated heuristics (perplexity delta, token overlap, hallucination detectors), 2) shadow traffic to a reranker for a random sample, and 3) prioritised human review on flagged critical queries. the heuristics give us fast signals, human review validates.
[03:52] Priya: what's the false positive rate on the heuristics? last time it flagged way too much.
[03:58] Marcus: right now ~12% FP with our tuned detector; we can tighten thresholds for canary to reduce noise, but that reduces sensitivity. I recommend keeping human-in-the-loop for the high-value queries.
[04:12] Lena: to be explicit, rollback triggers we propose: (a) 99th latency > baseline + 40% sustained for 10 minutes, (b) error rate > 0.5% absolute, (c) semantic regression metric on weighted eval set drops by >2.5 points, (d) SRE circuit breaker trip. any objections?
[04:30] Derek: fine though we may want 99th latency window of 5 minutes for faster action.
[04:36] Marcus: we can make that 5 minutes for the first two gates, keep the semantic regression on 15 minutes for stability.
[04:45] Priya: acceptable. are rollbacks automatic or manual?
[04:49] Lena: hybrid — automatic for circuit-breaker and error spikes, manual for semantic regressions unless the semantic metric is very severe. that avoids false-rollbacks from noisy heuristics.
[05:02] Tom: what about canary allocation strategy: AB or blue/green? we prefer sticky sessions for some endpoints.
[05:10] Marcus: we recommend a weighted A/B with session affinity optional. for endpoints needing stickiness we'll use blue/green for those paths. Mix and match by route is possible in the routing policy.
[05:24] Priya: any impact on KV cache for blue/green? earlier you mentioned KV cache warming concerns.
[05:30] Marcus: with blue/green you get cold KV cache for new variant so initial latency could be higher; we advise warming with shadow pre-warm traffic and some seeded KV entries. the runtime's continuous batching helps but warming will help meet SLOs.
[05:47] Derek: can Redwood perform prefix caching of common prompts for our top 20 routes?
[05:52] Marcus: yes, we can configure prefix/KV caching per-route. we'll suggest an initial cache policy; it reduces tokens and latency.
[06:00] Aisha: on compliance, we need audit logs and encryption in transit and at rest — do you support customer-managed keys?
[06:07] Lena: yes KMS integration supported; HSM option for private deployments. we'll include detail in the security packet.
[06:14] Priya: let's talk timeline — we want pilot go on 2026-08-27 if possible. is that feasible?
[06:20] Marcus: feasible if we finish runbook and dry-run next week; we need traffic profiles and the staging VPC by 2026-08-23.
[06:28] Tom: we can get the traffic extract by 8/20, SRE will stand up VPC peering by 8/23.
[06:34] Lena: great. Marcus, can you summarize the rollback steps verbally so Aisha is clear?
[06:40] Marcus: yes — step 1 detect gate violation, step 2 circuit breaker holds traffic to new model and route to fallback, step 3 automatic alert to on-call, step 4 if semantic regression, pause rollout and create incident, step 5 manual rollback to pinned older model, step 6 post-mortem with eval artifacts.
[06:56] Aisha: ok we need a runbook with contact list and escalation minutes for each step.
[07:02] Marcus: we'll include a runbook template with pager contacts and run link.
[07:08] Priya: about telemetry — what are the dashboards we should watch? latency percentiles, token cost, error rate, quality metric, user-visible errors — anything else?
[07:19] Marcus: add model selection splits, fallback counts, cache hit ratios, and token distribution by route. we'll provide a dashboard link.
[07:29] Tom: do you support alerting to PagerDuty or Slack?
[07:32] Lena: yes both; we'll provide recommended thresholds and include team's PD integration guide.
[07:38] Derek: small note: during the last test we saw a 30% token cost bump during the first hour of rollout due to longer generations. can we throttle generation or cap max tokens per route temporarily?
[07:49] Marcus: yes policy-level token caps per route and per-request max tokens are configurable; we'll propose conservative caps for the first 24 hours.
[07:58] Priya: if we detect hallucinations, do we have a safe-fallback to a deterministic retriever + reranker path?
[08:06] Marcus: yes, we can divert failed queries to a reranker stack or a retrieval-augmented pipeline; Redwood supports function-calling and structured outputs to tighten outputs.
[08:18] Lena: ok time check — we've got ~50 minutes left, let's walk through the concrete timeline and responsibilities then wrap.
[08:24] Marcus: timeline bullets: 8/20 traffic profile, 8/21 runbook and thresholds (Redwood), 8/23 staging VPC + pre-warm, 8/24 staging dry-run (5% for 4h), 8/25 review, 8/27 prod canary start.
[08:38] Priya: who will own the dry-run monitoring? we prefer joint ownership with our SRE and Redwood SE on call.
[08:45] Marcus: we will be on-call during dry-run; Redwood SE will also set automated alerting and shadow rerankers.
[08:52] Aisha: confirm we will not send PII to Redwood logs during tests? we need redaction.
[08:58] Lena: redaction can be applied client-side; we'll also apply event-only retention and provide a redaction hook.
[09:05] Tom: any dependencies from your side to start the dry-run?
[09:09] Marcus: only the VPC peering and a test API key with the routing policy. plus the traffic CSV to configure canary sample.
[09:16] Derek: VPC peering will include a egress NAT for metrics, we will send egress IPs.
[09:22] Priya: ok last question, are we able to do a canary that excludes clinical-critical endpoints entirely until late stage?
[09:30] Marcus: yes, route-level gating allows excluding critical routes until final stages. we'll annotate the routing policy accordingly.
[09:37] Lena: great. let's end with a recap and action items.

Summary / Recap:
- Agree on hybrid rollback model: automatic for infra/circuit-breaker and manual for semantic regressions unless severe.
- Canary ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> cut, with staging dry-run at 5% prior week.
- Gating metrics: 99th latency +40% (5 min), error rate 0.5%, semantic regression weighted eval >2.5 points.
- Security items: KMS integration, audit log retention, SSO/RBAC mapping.
- Timeline: traffic CSV due 8/20; Redwood runbook & thresholds 8/21; staging peering 8/23; staging dry-run 8/24; prod canary start 8/27.

Action Items (as agreed):
- Marcus Li (SE): canary thresholds and runbook draft (due 2026-08-21)
- Priya Nair: traffic profile and golden query set (due 2026-08-20)
- Aisha Clarke: security checklist confirmation and KMS details (due 2026-08-22)
- Derek Huang: staging VPC peering and egress IPs (due 2026-08-23)

Links referenced:
- Redwood runbook template (link to be shared by Redwood)
- Security packet (Redwood/security-deck)
- Canary threshold spreadsheet (to be attached)

Closing: Lena: thanks everyone, we'll send the runbook and the threshold spreadsheet by Friday, and let's reconvene after the dry-run for an ops review.
[65:00] Meeting end.
